# Asyntai

Asyntai puts an AI support agent on the user's website. The `asyntai` MCP
server that this plugin adds gives you the tools for that agent.

## First use: sign in

The server uses OAuth. If a tool call returns an authentication error, tell
the user to run `opencode mcp auth asyntai` in a terminal, or `/mcps` inside
OpenCode, and pick `asyntai`. A browser window opens once. Any Asyntai
account works, including the free plan.

## Start every task the same way

1. Call `list_websites`. Most accounts have one site; some have several.
2. If there are several, ask which one before any write. Write tools take a
   `website_id` and refuse to guess.
3. Read before you change: `get_ai_instructions` before editing
   instructions, `list_knowledge` before adding or removing knowledge.

## Common jobs

- **Teach the agent something**: `add_knowledge_text` for a fact, `add_knowledge_url` for a page.
- **Change how it answers**: `get_ai_instructions`, then `update_ai_instructions`.
- **See what visitors ask**: `list_conversations`, `get_conversation`, `list_knowledge_gaps`.
- **Leads**: `list_leads`.
- **Answer a visitor yourself**: `list_active_sessions`, `take_over_conversation`, `send_agent_reply`, `release_conversation`.
- **Plan and limits**: `get_account`, `list_plans`.
- **How does Asyntai work**: `search_asyntai_docs`, then `get_asyntai_doc`.

Tool names are exact; call `tools/list` if unsure. Read tools are safe to
call freely. Confirm with the user before deleting knowledge or changing
instructions on a live site.

# opencode-asyntai

OpenCode plugin for [Asyntai](https://asyntai.com), the AI support agent for
your website.

Asyntai puts an AI chatbot on your website that answers visitors from your own
content. This plugin connects OpenCode to your Asyntai account, so you can run
the chatbot from OpenCode: add knowledge, crawl a site, change the widget, read
conversations and leads, and reply live to visitors.

## Install

```bash
opencode plugin opencode-asyntai
```

Or add it to `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-asyntai"]
}
```

Then check the connection:

```bash
opencode mcp list
```

## Sign in

```bash
opencode mcp auth asyntai
```

Your browser opens the Asyntai sign-in page once. Any Asyntai account works,
including the free plan. [Create an account](https://asyntai.com/register/) if
you do not have one.

## What it adds

- The hosted Asyntai MCP server (`https://asyntai.com/mcp`) as `asyntai`.
- An `asyntai` skill that tells the agent how to use the tools safely.

A server named `asyntai` that you already set up yourself is kept as it is.

## Options

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-asyntai", { "name": "asyntai", "skills": true }]]
}
```

- `name`: the MCP server name. Default `asyntai`.
- `url`: the MCP server address. Default `https://asyntai.com/mcp`.
- `skills`: set to `false` to leave out the skill.

## Try it

- "Create an Asyntai chatbot for shop.example.com and give me the embed code."
- "Add the text in docs/faq.md to my chatbot's knowledge."
- "Show me what visitors asked my chatbot this week."

Full guide: https://asyntai.com/documentation/integrations/opencode/
